# Scenario: Commodity Supercycle

## Trigger
- Multiple commodities simultaneously above 10Y averages
- Mining/energy capex at multi-decade lows as % of GDP
- Major new demand source (energy transition, India industrialization)
- Supply constraints: mine depletion, resource nationalism, ESG restrictions
- Inventories across base metals at cycle lows

## Macro Assumptions

| Variable | Baseline | 3-Year | 5-Year |
|----------|---------|--------|--------|
| Copper (USD/tonne) | $X,XXX | +30% | +50% |
| Oil (WTI) | $XX | +20% | +15% (demand destruction) |
| Iron Ore | $XX | +15% | +10% |
| Lithium (USD/tonne LCE) | $XX,XXX | +40% | +60% |
| Commodity FX (AUD, NZD, CAD, BRL) | — | +10-20% | +15-25% |
| Global CPI | X.X% | +0.5pp | +1pp |
| Mining Capex / GDP | X.X% | +50% | +100% |

## Transmission Channels

### Inflation Channel
- Commodity price passthrough → global CPI +0.5-1.5pp
- Second-round effects: wage demands in commodity sectors → services inflation
- Central banks forced to hold rates higher for longer (commodity inflation is supply-driven — harder for CBs to control)

### Currency Channel
- AUD, NZD, CAD, BRL, CLP, ZAR all strengthen significantly
- USD weakens (commodities priced in USD, inverse relationship)
- EM manufacturing importers (INR, TRY, PHP) face import cost pressure
- Carry trade: long commodity currencies, fund with JPY/CHF

### Fiscal Channel
- Commodity exporting nations: fiscal windfall (Chile copper revenue, Saudi oil, Australia iron ore)
- Sovereign wealth funds accumulate (GPFG, Future Fund, CIC)
- Importing nations: subsidy pressure (India fuel, Egypt food)

### Sector Impact
| Sector | Impact | Driver |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Mining / Metals | 🟢 +30-50% | Direct beneficiary |
| Energy | 🟢 +20-40% | Direct beneficiary |
| Mining Services / Equipment | 🟢 +25-40% | Capex cycle |
| Industrials (commodity-exposed) | 🟡 0 to +15% | Mixed — input costs vs demand |
| Consumer Discretionary | 🔴 -5 to -15% | Inflation squeeze |
| Airlines | 🔴 -10 to -20% | Jet fuel costs |
| EM Equities (commodity exporters) | 🟢 +15-25% | Terms of trade |
| EM Equities (commodity importers) | 🔴 -10 to -20% | Import cost squeeze |

## Key Beneficiary Countries
1. Australia (iron ore, coal, LNG)
2. Brazil (iron ore, soy, oil)
3. Chile (copper, lithium)
4. Canada (oil, gas, metals)
5. Saudi Arabia / UAE (oil)
6. Indonesia (coal, nickel, palm oil)

## Key Monitoring Triggers
- [ ] Global copper inventories < 3 weeks of demand
- [ ] Mining capex / GDP at multi-year lows
- [ ] Multiple commodities simultaneously above 90th percentile (5Y)
- [ ] China + India combined commodity demand growth > 5% YoY
- [ ] Producer equity valuations implying commodity prices far below spot (mispricing)
